result:
Solution 2 (f(q) = 2q − 2) is my best guess, and I have not derived it. My reasoning is partly from memory of the literature and partly a plausibility check.

**Why not Solution 3 (q − 1).** In the compact case with a fibration over a curve of genus q and elliptic fibres, p_g ≥ q − 1 is sharp. It is attained by a bielliptic-type quotient with a nontrivial torsion line bundle on the base. That is the compact bound, though, and the problem asks about the logarithmic setting. I believe the log result is stronger than q − 1, so I rejected Solution 3.

**Why not Solution 1 (2q − 3).** I recall the compact-surface inequality as p_g ≥ 2q − 4 for non-maximal Albanese dimension, not 2q − 3. I could not connect 2q − 3 to any log analogue, so I rejected it.

**Why Solution 2.** I vaguely recall the log paper stating \(\overline P_1(V) \ge 2\overline q(V) - 2\) in the non-maximal Albanese dimension case. My plausibility check is a fibration over an open curve of genus g with n punctures. There \(\overline q\) is about g + n − 1, and \(\overline P_1\) is bounded below by the dimension of the space of log forms on the base, which has degree 2g − 2 + n. That count is consistent with a bound of the form 2q − 2, but it does not prove it.

CHOICE: 2
